fields.value: Handsome, polished, and immediately engaging in address.
Charming, adaptable, resentful, self-indulgent, and skilled at turning partial truth into persuasive grievance.
To secure pleasure, money, status, and revenge while avoiding responsibility for past choices.
Son of Pemberley’s late steward; educated with Darcy’s support and once intended for a church living.
Not stated precisely; near Darcy’s generation.
Militia officer; later receives a commission in the regular army.
False romantic alternative and catalyst for the novel’s major reputational crisis.
Godson of Darcy’s father; son of the former Pemberley steward.
Moves with the militia; later stationed in the north with Lydia.
His appealing surface is progressively separated from his conduct; the marriage to Lydia limits scandal without reforming him.
Darcy: childhood connection turned grievance. Elizabeth: wins and loses her confidence. Lydia: elopes and marries. Georgiana: attempted elopement in the past.
